title: Install bottleneck handoff and ops notes — Aug 06 2026
content:
Goal: capture today’s standup + focused handoff for the Acadia on-prem install. This doc is intentionally lightweight — use as the single source for next-steps we agreed on Aug 06, 2026.

Attendees:
- Ravi Menon (install lead)
- Leah Chen (networking)
- Diego Morales (ops/on-site)
- Saira Ahmed (telemetry + observability)
- Jonah Baker (platform oncall)
- Maya Patel (Acadia SE, remote)

Summary (top 3):
1) Customer impact: Acadia experiencing intermittent tokenization timeouts during high-concurrency synthetic load; customer pacing their triage until we fix a likely network MTU/fragmentation issue.
2) Root-cause hypothesis: two possible contributors — (A) MTU mismatch between edge router and customer Core switch causing dropped fragments for >1400B payloads, (B) our sidecar health-probe timing in combination with packet loss causing repeated reconnects and KV-cache invalidations.
3) Immediate mitigation: disable large-payload batching and increase probe interval to 15s for the affected pool; roll as hotfix to their staging first.

Detailed notes / timeline:
- 08:30 standup: Diego reported 3 failure windows overnight (peak 03:10, 05:44, 06:33 UTC). Failures correlate with client bursts ~2–3k rps.
- 09:00 telemetry review: Saira shows increased retransmits on interface eth0 on customer edge boxes (P95 increase 4x). Application logs show repeated KV-cache flush during those windows.
- 10:15 network debugging call (Leah + Maya): pulled tcpdump on both sides. Observed ICMP fragmentation-needed messages from core->edge. Edge router MTU 1500, some middlebox doing MSS clamping to 1400, but core switches have offload enabled that fragments earlier.
- 11:05 ops runbook attempt: Diego applied temporary rate-limiter on ingress (cap 800 rps) — observed brief stability but unacceptable latency for Acadia test scenarios.

Hypotheses and evidence:
- H1 (MTU mismatch): tcpdump shows fragmented packets and ICMP frag-needed. Consistent with failure windows and large-payload requests failing first. Evidence strong.
- H2 (sidecar probe sensitivity): sidecar logs show reconnects within 8s of packet loss which triggers downstream state clearing. Probe interval default 5s may be too aggressive for noisy links. Evidence moderate.
- H3 (CPU-quantization interaction): low probability, included due to one previous case where quantized model + high concurrency caused CPU scheduling stalls. No CPU spikes observed here.

Immediate action items (owners and ETA):
- Leah: validate MTU path using pmtu and traceroute --mtu from Acadia edge to our gateway. Report by EOD 2026-08-06. (PD-4821)
- Diego: prepare hotfix build that disables large-payload batching and sets sidecar probe interval to 15s. Create canary lane and smoke test doc. Target deploy to Acadia staging 2026-08-07 03:00 UTC. (owner-runbook: deploy-hotfix-acadia)
- Saira: create a short-lived dashboard (widget) that shows packet retransmits + KV-cache flush count and set an alert at 5x baseline. Share link in Slack and add to oncall rotation. ETA 4 hours. (PD-4890)
- Jonah: standby for rollback plan and ensure RBAC for fast rollback is ready (pre-allocated rollback playbook + contacts). ETA EOD 2026-08-06.
- Ravi: consolidate notes, confirm customer communication, and run the pre-deploy checklist with Diego. ETA immediate (before 02:00 UTC deploy).

Open blockers / escalation plan:
- Customer networking team needs a scheduled maintenance window to change MTU on core. If they cannot, Leah to propose a hybrid packet-shaping config on our edge to avoid fragmentation.
- If hotfix fails in staging, we will pivot to route-by-policy to move Acadia traffic to older model variant that uses short payloads. That is a non-ideal UX but quick if needed.

Telemetry + logs (what to watch during canary):
- Interface retransmits (eth0 pps) and ICMP frag-needed counts.
- KV-cache flushes per replica (expect drop to near-zero if network issue resolved).
- Sidecar reconnect rate and full connection duration distribution.
- Tail latency P99 before and after change (goal: <300ms delta).

On-site checklist items (for Diego):
- Confirm PSU and switch firmware versions match the compatibility matrix.
- Verify jumbo frame support (if we go that route) end-to-end.
- Have spare SFPs and spare NIC on hand.
- Bring USB with prebuilt diagnostic scripts (net-mtu-check, pcap-rollup).

Customer comms draft (Ravi to send after Leah signoff):
- Short note acknowledging root cause hypothesis and immediate mitigations + expected ETA for staging test. Ask for permission to schedule maintenance if required. Keep tone: transparent + prioritized.

Notes to self / developer scribbles:
- If fragmentation is root cause, long-term: add adaptive MTU/probing in our egress path and fallback to smaller batch sizes automatically when frag-needed observed.
- Consider a 'no-large-batch' runtime flag for onprem customers to avoid emergency hotfixes.

Decisions captured:
- Do hotfix canary deploy to staging (agreed).
- Do not throttle customer production until canary passes.

Follow-ups (next meeting 2026-08-07 09:00 UTC):
- Leah: MTU path confirmation + mitigation option doc.
- Diego: canary deploy results + rollback readiness.
- Saira: dashboard link and initial alert firing status.
- Jonah: confirmation that RBAC and rollback playbook are set.

Unresolved questions:
- Is there any intermediate NAT device doing MSS clamping we missed? (Leah investigating)
- Could application-level retries be tuned to avoid cache clears during short bursts? (product/serving runtime question)

Quick TL;DR for slack: "Acadia onprem: suspected MTU fragmentation causing KV-cache invalidations under burst load. Hotfix (disable large-batch + increase probe interval) to staging 8/7; monitoring and rollback ready. Leah investigating MTU path. PD-4821/PD-4890."

Attachments (uploaded to the meeting thread):
- pcap snippets (redacted)
- quick canary smoke test steps (document link in linked_artifacts)
- short customer-facing note (draft)

-- end --

This doc should be used as the single place for owners to update the status. Keep edits small and date-stamped; avoid adding large new sections without a short summary at the top.
